OFFICIAL

Dear list,

I have been trying to resubmit my package MBHdesign to CRAN.  It passes --check-as-cran on both the current release and the devel release. However, it is not passing the incoming checks to CRAN.  The check log is pasted below.

1) My email domain has changed (from @data61.csiro.au to @csiro.au) but I will receive email to both but only send from the latter. It was my understanding that this is probably the problem previously.  I emailed CRAN-submissions at R-project.org to ask for advice, but did not receive anything back.
2) The log states that the package was removed from CRAN. This means that the current submission is a new submission.  Yet I'm still getting the note and the rejection. Does that mean that it isn't an email address problem?

What is the pathway to fixing this note?  Any help is appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Scott

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] how to suppress undesired messages
messages.body_plain:
Hello,  Mike.

Thanks for your kind advice and apologies for my *very* late reply. It so happened that when your message arrived, it was automatically moved from the email inbox to my R-pkg-develop mailbox, but somehow I did not spot it until now. I have no explantion for this, ...except that this looks like a case of ageing effect!

I have now made the changes that you suggested. Specifically, in the DESCRIPTION file, there are these lines

Depends: R (>= 4.2.0),
Imports: sn (>= 2.1.3), ggplot2 (>= 3.4.2), methods, mnormt (>= 2.1.2),  patchwork (>= 1.1.2) 

and in NAMESPACE there is

import(sn)
import(ggplot2)

Unfortunately, when I run  R CMD check --as-cran  gg.sn_0.1.1.tar.gz, I now get an error message whenever an example of the documentation uses a function of package sn, such as 

> f1 <- makeSECdistr(dp=c(3,2,5), family="SN", name="First-SN")
Error in makeSECdistr(dp = c(3, 2, 5), family = "SN", name = "First-SN") :    could not find function ?makeSECdistr"

Even if I include a line like

importFrom(sn, dp2cp, makeSECdistr, modeSECdistr, marginalSECdistr)  

in NAMESPACE, still the error persists.

The only solution which worked was to write 
f1 <- sn::makeSECdistr(dp=c(3,2,5), family="SN", name="First-SN?)
but this make the usage and coding less smooth.

Am I missing something? 

Best regards,

Adelchi



> On 16 Apr 2026, at 22:25, Michael Chirico <michaelchirico4 at gmail.com> wrote:
> 
> Hey Adelchi,
> 
> Why do you have sn and ggplot2 as Depends? My own very strong opinion is that authors of new packages should never use it.
> 
> Move them to Imports, and use 'import(sn)' and 'import(ggplot2)' in your NAMESPACE if you really want the whole packages.
> 
> Mike C
> 
> On Thu, Apr 16, 2026 at 8:15?AM Adelchi Azzalini <azzalini at stat.unipd.it> wrote:
> Hi. I am preparing a new package, called gg.sn, which in essence provides ggplot2-style graphics as a replacement for the existing graphics produced by package sn.  The new package works by loading new functions and methods with the same names and calling statements of those in package sn (after sn has been loaded), effectively superseding them with the new ones.
> 
> My current task is to get rid of a spate of undesired messages which appear at start-up of gg.sn, as show in the list copied at the end of this message; the line numbers have been added for helping referencing the lines.
> 
> For lines 3 to 5, I know where they come from: they are start-up messages from ?sn?; so I can drop them, since I am the author of sn. All the rest is outside my control. Question: is it possible to get rid of these other messages and, in case, how?
> 
> The DESCRIPTION file includes these lines:
> Depends: R (>= 4.2.0), sn (>= 2.1.3),  ggplot2 (>= 3.4.2) 
> Imports: methods, mnormt (>= 2.1.2), patchwork (>= 1.1.2) 
> 
> Given these declarations, there are no loading commands to which I could possibly apply suppressPackageStartupMessages().
> 
> Also, there is no start-up message issued by gg.sn, whose .onAttach function only contains  
> .onAttach <- function(library, pkg)
> {
>  if(interactive())
>   {
>     meta <- packageDescription("gg.sn?)
>   } 
>  invisible()
> }
> 
> apart from various comment lines.
> 
> Best regards.
> 
> ---
> Adelchi Azzalini
> http://azzalini.stat.unipd.it
> 
> 
>  0 R> library(gg.sn)
>  1 Loading required package: sn
>  2 Loading required package: stats4
>  3 Package 'sn', 2.1.3 (2026-02-24).

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] Generalize checkBuilt parameter to built date
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-devel] Generalize checkBuilt parameter to built date
messages.body_plain:
A while ago there was discussion on this list about new behavior in
R-4.6 of update.packages to reinstall packages if the "Built"
timestamp has changed. This leads to many unnecessary updates for e.g.
Windows users because CRAN rebuilds most Windows binary packages every
few days.

Maybe it makes sense to let users opt-in to this behavior via the
existing 'checkBuilt' parameter. This would be a trivial change:
https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/338/changes
